newsitem.title: USA: CBOT appoints new task force on grain storage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT appoints new task force on grain storage.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade announced a new task force to propose solutions to the problem of shrinking elevator storage capacity for delivery against its corn and soybeans futures contracts.
The five-member committee consists of the following:
- Dan Amstutz, North American Grain Export Association
- Craig Pirrong, Washington University, St Louis
Evans and Kottke will co-chair the task force.

"We hope for a timely resolution as it relates to the long-term viability of the entire grain delivery system for our premier grain contracts," CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said in a statement announcing the panel.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said on December 19 that the delivery terms of the CBOT's corn and soybean contracts no longer met the statutory objectives in the Commodity Exchange Act, due to elevator closures.
CFTC expressed concerns about potential for market manipulation and ordered CBOT to submit a plan to raise the capacity and number of locations for grain delivery.
The CBOT must submit a plan to the CFTC by mid-March.

"We now face a situation where the contracts have a combined open interest of three billion bushels and storage capacity somewhere in the vicinity of 15 million bushels," CFTC commissioner Barbara Holum said in December.
Arbor also appointed an advisory council to the grain storage task force, consisting of more than 50 CBOT grain traders, grain industry executives and industry associations.
In October 1996, CBOT members rejected a CBOT board plan to allow corn, soybeans and wheat to be delivered against futures in Milwaukee and at points along the Illinois River.
That plan also proposed eliminating St Louis as a delivery point but keeping Chicago and Toledo.
